content: warren-fb32 / #487: scenarios 27 + 31 now initialize the bound Plot at 'ready' (not pre-seeded 'active') and assert the dispatch-time ready->active promotion (promotePlotToActiveOnDispatch, warren-dfff) via the shared assertPlotPromotedToActiveOnDispatch helper in scripts/acceptance/scenarios/lib/event-helpers.ts: the snapshot reaches 'active' AND a status_changed->active by user:operator lands on disk, before the final child merge flips it to 'done'. The promotion only logs (plan_run.plot_activated/_skipped/_failed) and does NOT emit a plan-run event, so proof lives in the Plot event log, not fetchAllPlanRunEvents.

description: Scenario 37 (K8s OOM fast-fail) against GKE fails with 'last state=running' when the fixture project's .warren/config.yaml asks for memoryMiB below the schema floor: ResourcesConfigSchema enforces min 64 MiB, so a 32 MiB fixture is REJECTED at load (log tell: scheduler.warren_config_errors count=1 for the project, level=info so easy to miss) and the run silently falls back to the 4Gi default limit — the agent never OOMs. Budget note: first dispatch on a cold Autopilot cluster eats ~100s in PVC provisioning + node scale-up + first image pull, so scenario 37's 120s deadline only holds on a warmed cluster.
resolution: Set the fixture repo's memoryMiB to exactly 64 (the floor) — still OOMs the bun+node agent startup in seconds; GKE run reached failed(oom_killed) in ~16s. Warm the cluster (one prior dispatch) before trusting the 120s deadline.

description: compose image: flip silently defeats --build in container-mode acceptance
resolution: The acceptance compose override re-adds its own build: section (warren:acceptance tag) when opts.build !== false

name: self-booting-acceptance-scenario
description: An acceptance scenario can boot its own warren via bootInProc on a private mkdtemp with a DB seeded through warren's repos before boot; terminal runs mean no bridge resume, so the scenario needs no burrow dispatch and is CI-cheap (scenario 39).

content: Derive a leak guard's route set from API_ROUTE_POLICIES and its forbidden-field set from the exported REDACTED_* constants; hand-copied lists were already stale (warren-946f widened REDACTED_RUN_FIELDS past its original four names). Each redacted column also carries a unique sentinel value so a rename can't slip a leak past.

title: No blanket 'no Bearer on the wire' assertion
rationale: The scrubber deliberately keeps the header prefix and writes 'Bearer [redacted]', and several 403 hints say 'operator bearer token'; match bearer\s+(?!\[redacted\])[\w.\-+/=~]{12,} instead.
